instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, I packed my tools in a red bag like yours. Ready for the museum job. Tell me you're pleased I'm going.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Red means they're going for repair. You're thirty; you don't need my permission to leave the workshop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, get them ready. I want the person who taught me to make things to think the museum counts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll keep your tools here. You might want to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpen them for the museum instead, would you? Send me off expecting me to do well.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, I've initialled the lease like you. That makes two votes for our new home. Say it's good news before I open the wine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I signed as a witness. You don't need permission from me to live with Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, witnessed. I still want my mother to be pleased about living with Sam.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm pleased for you. I'm still getting used to Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you toast both of us, then? It's Sam's home too.

cards.title: Carry This with Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put N/A on Mum's care-home forms like you. Take half; being her children can't mean I'm the paperwork child.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: N/A means it doesn't apply. I put it under driving licence; you've put it under medication.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, leave room for the medicines. Sit beside me and read the questions out; we'll decide together before you write anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. It only allows one main contact.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put yourself. I'll sit with you for the first call; you shouldn't have to handle it alone either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've bundled our letters like yours. That's the choosing done; take half before the removal van comes. We both filled this box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tied mine so they wouldn't fall out. I haven't chosen what to keep.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, ready for the van. Sit with me and we'll choose together; I can't decide what ten years means on my own.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box. I just can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose a day we'll open it together. I don't want you deciding what to keep on your own either.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ticked the same hotel box as you for your sister's wedding. Shall I ask for a double bed for us?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ticked step-free access for Mum. We can share a room to save money, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, access first. Double or twin beds, then?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Twins. I've told my sister you're coming with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When they gather the family for photographs, do I wait beside you or find a seat with the other guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded my towel beside yours. Nice and ready for visitors. Shall I put my washbag in the guest cupboard too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I folded mine because the hook broke. Your old towel is still on your hook.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the broken hook. Shall I use the old towel when I stay tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use it. I haven't given that space to anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I leave, do you want it back on my hook or with the guest laundry?

cards.title: Take My Side
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into your interpretation of a conflict involving a shared relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I threw out the ticket envelope like you. When Mum asks about the holiday argument, tell her I offered to drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine was empty. You threw away the tickets; that's why you had to offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the envelopes. Tell her about the offer first; she needs to hear I tried to help.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm telling her the whole story, including the tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Include them. Just start with me offering to get everyone there, then explain why we needed the car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I crossed off alternate allotment Saturdays like you. Tell Alex we're sharing the work fairly; you're his friend too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I crossed off one Saturday for a funeral. We agreed all three of us would go together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, making room for other commitments. Help him see my version as giving everyone some weekends back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll talk to him, but you have to admit you changed our agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will. Could you tell him I changed it because I want us to stay friends, not spend every Saturday resenting one another?

cards.title: Prove We’re Close
cards.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Link your arm through mine again, like you did on the steps. We'll walk into the reunion together and let them see us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took your arm because I slipped. They still think we're just friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Keep hold now we're on level ground; I want us to trust each other in that room too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time someone asked, you let go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my partner. Will you keep your arm in mine while I say it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've sent 'fine' like you. We make everything sound so easy. Tell me what you deleted; you can say the awkward part to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant the parking was fine. I deleted the rest because it sounded needy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, parking sorted. Send the needy part to me; I'd like to be someone you can say it to.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You first. You always sound so casual.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I check whether you've replied before I get out of bed. Will you send me the part you were afraid I'd mind?
